name: vLLM disaggregated PD serving: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on GB200 NVL72, 25K total TPS per GPU
unit: total tokens/s per GPU (aggregate across the rack)
methodology: Engine: vLLM nightly-d223c90 (vllm/vllm-openai) with async scheduling, served under disaggregated prefill/decode via NVIDIA Dynamo 1.2.0.dev20260526 and srt-slurm v1.0.32. Hardware: GB200 NVL72 cluster on one NVLink72 domain. Prompt length ISL = 8192, output length OSL = 1024, synthetic random dataset with random_range_ratio=0.8. Concurrency SWEPT from 64 to 5120; 25,000 tok/s/GPU is the best point on the resulting Pareto frontier, not a single fixed-concurrency measurement - the exact concurrency behind the headline lives in a PNG figure, so the source omits the specific batch size. Decode side fixed at one DEP8 endpoint (data parallel + expert parallel over 8 GPUs); prefill side swept over 4-8 DEP2 endpoints. Tensor-parallel size: not a single TP value - the deployment uses DEP (DP + EP) on decode and DEP2 on prefill. Figure is AGGREGATE total tokens/s per GPU across the rack, counting both prompt and generated tokens; prefix caching disabled, stream-interval 100. GSM8K accuracy 88% verified per configuration.
notes:
Authored on NVIDIA-run GB200 hardware by vLLM/NVIDIA/Inferact contributors; treat as vendor-published even though the tooling and recipes are open source. Reproducible in practice: the exact Docker digest, Dynamo and srt-slurm versions are named, and every recipe is published in NVIDIA/srt-slurm-recipes under recipes/multi-node/Qwen3.5/GB200/8k1k/vllm/disagg with a single `srtctl run` command. The 25K figure is a rounded headline read off a Pareto chart, so treat it as ~25K, not a precise measurement. --stream-interval 100 buffers output in 100-token chunks, which inflates apparent per-token latency - do not use this record for ITL/TPOT.
